conviction_note: Two company-level primary-document signals lean up: Q2 adjusted EBITDA beat its own guide by 11-15% while revenue landed inside its range, and the board authorised a $15m buyback (about 15% of a ~$100m market cap) on 2026-10-20, three weeks after Q3 closed and a week before the print. Against that, revenue consensus ($11.13-11.2m) sits above the top of the $10.85-11.05m Q3 guide, the FY revenue guide implies a Q4 step-up that the ARR trajectory only just supports, and the stock is already +14.8% in five sessions on the buyback. abs_move 10 (median reaction 7.54, with 37.5 and -22.4 in the last five prints, ~$600k a day of turnover, Q4 outlook in the release); p_up 57 because the lean rests on primary documents but is partly priced by the run-up. Scaled 0.14 x 10 = +1.4; findings sum +1.4, so the two measurements agree here, by arithmetic and not by fitting.

findings.finding: AudioEye's board authorised a new $15m share repurchase (through 2027-10-18) on 2026-10-20, replacing a $12.5m 2025 programme of which only $475k was used in Q1 2026; $15m is roughly 15% of the ~$100m market cap (12.57m shares x ~$8) and 1.7x the $8.7m cash at June 30, announced after Q3 had closed (Sept 30) and one week before the Q3 print, with the CEO saying 'we expect to generate meaningful cash over the next year as operating leverage continues to increase'. A management that knows its Q3 numbers is unlikely to size a buyback at 1.7x cash a week before a weak print; leverage covenant (funded debt/adj EBITDA <= 2.5x from 2026-09-30) sits at about 1.7x on $16.8m debt, so the buyback is not covenant-constrained.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior buyback announced this close to a print. The stock has risen +14.8% in the five sessions since the 8-K (baseline run_up_5d_pct), which is the market's own reaction to this line. The Aug 2026 print, where management first said it was 'evaluating buybacks and dividends' alongside an EBITDA raise, moved +37.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The announcement itself is priced (the 5-day run-up). What is not priced is the read-through: the timing implies management saw Q3 cash generation and the Q4 outlook before committing 1.7x its June cash. If the market had priced that inference fully, the stock would be back near its post-Aug highs and sell-side targets ($12-16, last set in March) would have been refreshed; neither has happened.
findings.independence: Q2 release (separate document, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926095913/aeye-20260813xex99d1.htm) guided 'meaningful free cash flow generation in the second half of 2026' and >$15m run-rate EBITDA; same management, so partly the same voice. Covenant terms from the Q2 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926096032/aeye-20260630x10q.htm

findings.finding: AudioEye has beaten its own adjusted-EBITDA guide while landing revenue inside its range: Q2 2026 adj EBITDA $3.0m against a $2.6-2.7m guide (+11-15%) on revenue of $10.72m against $10.65-10.75m, and Q1 2026 the company said it 'exceeded adjusted EBITDA guidance'; the Q3 guide is $3.4-3.6m adj EBITDA and the FY guide (>= $12.7m) needs Q4 >= ~$3.9m, so a repeat of the Q2 pattern prints Q3 EBITDA near $3.8-4.0m and invites a second FY EBITDA raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-13): EBITDA beat its guide by 11-15% and FY EBITDA guide raised from >= $12m to >= $12.7m; stock +37.5% over the window. Q1 2026 (pre-released 2026-04-27, 'exceeded EBITDA guidance'): -1.8%, then -5.3% on the full release 2026-05-12. Mixed: the line has paid once big and once not at all.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 bar on EBITDA is the company's own guide and the EPS consensus is disputed ($0.23 vs $0.26), so no estimate source carries a beat above the guide. Six analysts, price targets untouched since March; if a repeat beat were priced the stock would sit above its post-Q2 level, not 48% off its 52-week high.
findings.independence: Q2 guide for comparison from the Q1 release, a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926059428/aeye-20260512xex99d1.htm. The buyback finding points the same way but is a different document and a different line.

findings.finding: Sell-side Q3 revenue consensus ($11.13m Benzinga, $11.2m MarketBeat) sits above the top of the company's $10.85-11.05m guide, while AudioEye's revenue has landed inside its guided range (Q2 $10.72m vs $10.65-10.75m); a guide-midpoint print of ~$10.95-11.0m is a ~1-1.5% revenue miss against the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Aug 2026 Earnings Whispers characterised the FY revenue guide as 'below estimates' and the stock still rose +37.5% on the EBITDA raise: revenue misses of ~1% have not been the line this name trades on recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Headline-scanning will read revenue vs $11.13-11.2m consensus and print 'miss' even though the number is inside guidance; the consensus figures shown have not been cut down into the guide range, which they would have been if the street had absorbed the guide.
findings.independence: Benzinga estimate $11.13m against the same guide: https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/AEYE/financials (independent estimate source, same guide).

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide ($43.5-44.0m) less H1 actual ($21.32m) less the Q3 guide midpoint ($10.95m) implies Q4 revenue of $11.23-11.73m (midpoint $11.48m, +$530k sequential), against a Q3 guided step of only +$235k and ARR adds of ~$1.1-1.2m a quarter (ARR $40.0m Dec -> $41.2m Mar -> $42.3m Jun), which supports roughly +$300k a quarter of subscription revenue; the Q4 outlook in this release is more likely to point to the low end of FY revenue than the midpoint, unless Q3 ARR accelerated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: March 2026 print (FY2026 first guide) -22.4%; Aug 2026 FY revenue 'tightened' to $43.5-44.0m from $43.25-44.25m (midpoint up $0) while EBITDA raised: +37.5%. FY revenue has been held, not cut, so far.
findings.why_not_priced: Arithmetic inference from company guides; no aggregator shows the implied Q4 step-up, and FY revenue consensus ($43.9m per MarketBeat) sits near the guide midpoint, i.e. the street has not shaded toward the low end. Inference, not a document, so sized small.
findings.independence: ARR series from the Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926059428/aeye-20260512xex99d1.htm) - same company, separate document. One third-party summary says management anticipates Q4 sequential acceleration, which cuts against this finding and is why it is small.

findings.finding: GAAP results have been dragged by litigation: $1.1m litigation expense in Q1 and again in Q2 2026 (G&A up, Q2 net loss $(0.9)m, opex +23%), with the 10-Q giving no case detail; a third consecutive ~$1m charge would keep GAAP EPS negative while adjusted metrics beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 GAAP loss of $(0.17)/share 'primarily due to higher litigation expenses of $1.1m': stock -5.3% on that release, but the guide was the bigger driver; Q2 GAAP loss of $(0.07) did not stop +37.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Below the adjusted line the name trades on; no stated path to the guide. Kept tiny for that reason.
findings.independence: Q2 10-Q MD&A attributes G&A rise to higher litigation expense: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926096032/aeye-20260630x10q.htm (same company, same quarter - one fact).

findings.finding: Customer concentration rose in Q2 2026: two customers were 23% of Q2 revenue (13% and 10%) where only one exceeded 10% over the six months, consistent with Partner & Marketplace revenue +16% y/y (59% of ARR) while Enterprise revenue was flat; a growing partner is the growth engine and also the single largest exposure into Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned visibly on a single partner; the Partner channel's +16% accompanied the +37.5% August reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Concentration sits in the 10-Q notes, not in the release or the wire; the partners are unnamed. Two-sided, so sized near zero: net of the rest (Enterprise ~41% of ARR, flat), the partner channel has carried all of the growth.
findings.independence: Partner +16% / Enterprise flat from MarketBeat's call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/audioeye-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-13/) - same underlying company disclosure.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with; my lean is positive and in the same direction as the +14.8% five-day run-up, which means part of it is priced, so p_up is held at 57 rather than the 60s that the primary-document evidence alone would support.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1/6 (revenue consensus above guide): the name has not traded on ~1% revenue misses (Aug +37.5% with revenue guide below street), so the revenue-vs-consensus finding went from -1.0 to -0.6.
Lesson 5 (inference/covenant-style arithmetic loses to documents): the implied-Q4 revenue step-up finding shrank from -1.0 to -0.7.
Lesson 2 (one-offs below the line): litigation expense shrank from -0.3 to -0.1.

Lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxy): Title II delay shrank from -0.3 to -0.2; positioning/run-up finding from -0.5 to -0.3 (lesson 5 on positioning not being a cause, lesson 7 short interest checked and not crowded).
